newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Highlands ready to study Ramu nickel find.
newsitem.headline: Highlands ready to study Ramu nickel find.

text.p: Highlands Pacific Ltd said on Monday it was now able to start in July an 18-month program covering a feasibility study and pre-development and environmental work on the Ramu nickel/cobalt project in Papua New Guinea after naming consulting engineers to the project.
"The appointments cover the four key areas of the study and include a Fluour Daniel/H.A. Simons joint venture as the principal engineer and consultant to lead the study," Highlands said.

NSR Environmental Consultants were named to provide environmental services to the proposed mine because of the firm's extensive experience in mountainous tropical terrains, Highlands said. H.A. Simons design nickel and cobalt processing plants, it added.

Highlands has proposed developing the Ramu nickel/cobalt and Freida River copper/gold projects in PNG, while continuing exploration work on mineral deposits in other parts of the South Pacific nation and in Indonesia.

Highlands Pacific was born from a restructuring by Highlands Gold Ltd after a successful takeover offer by Canadian miner Placer Dome Inc late last year that hived off Highlands' 25 percent stake in the Porgera gold mine.
The Ramu resource is estimated to contain 1.1 million tonnes of nickel and 0.1 million tonnes of cobalt.
Highlands holds a 65-percent stake in the Ramu project. The Nord Pacific Group arm of Nord Resources Corp has the other 35 percent.
